title: 747-8F Load Planner
summary: Where the containers go on a freighter decides where its centre of gravity sits, and the centre of gravity drives fuel burn. This planner lets you drag ULDs onto a 747-8F, watch the CG move, lock what you want to keep, and let an optimiser place the rest — solved in your browser.

facts.label: Role
facts.value: Team lead / PM & UI — problem framing, interface, MILP research

facts.label: Scope
facts.value: 34 positions · 3 load scenarios · weight limits · type compatibility · lateral balance

facts.label: Stack
facts.value: React 19 · TypeScript · dnd-kit · GLPK via WebAssembly in a Web Worker

sections.heading: The problem
paragraphs: A load plan is a decision with a lot of fuel behind it, yet the planning we saw was informal. A planner needs to see the aircraft, move things by hand, and have a machine handle the arithmetic of where the rest should go so the CG lands on target.

sections.heading: Drag, lock, solve
paragraphs: Drag a ULD onto a position; invalid targets — over the weight limit, wrong type for a nose bay — are flagged before you drop, and the CG gauge updates live. Lock any position and press Solve: the model treats it as fixed and plans everything else around it.

sections.heading: The model, in one paragraph
paragraphs: Every ULD–position pair that fits gets a binary variable. Each ULD is placed exactly once, each position used at most once, locked pairs are fixed. The longitudinal CG is linear because total weight is a constant; deviation from target and lateral imbalance are linearised and minimised together. The full case solves in well under a second in the browser, and the formulation is shown on screen in the How-it-works drawer.
